items.title: Lazy Agents Answer Against Their Own Beliefs: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs Teaches Them to Act on What They Believe
items.summary: AI agents working on long tasks often commit to an answer before they have enough evidence, a behavior called laziness. In our evaluations, they frequently commit even while their stated belief still names several possible answers. An outcome reward at the end of the episode scores only the final answer, so it cannot teach the agent when to commit, because a lucky guess receives the same reward as an answer backed by evidence. During training, however, the simulator can compute the exact posterior over the answer at every step and tell whether the evidence is already enough. We propose Reinfo…

items.source: dair-ai Top AI Papers of the Week (November 16 - November 22) - 2026
items.title: Self-Improvement Memory
items.summary: Harness optimization is usually studied with one fixed model and one fixed benchmark. When either changes, the optimizer has to decide which parts of an evolved harness to keep, but the harness code alone does not record why earlier edits were made or how they performed. Researchers from Google Cloud AI, Google DeepMind, and Penn State study this setting, which they call continual recursive self-improvement, and give the harness optimizer its own memory.

items.title: PartAgent: Agentic 3D Part Segmentation via Expert Integration and Closed-Loop Refinement
items.summary: Segmenting a 3D object into semantically meaningful parts requires joint reasoning about geometric structure and semantic context. Pretrained 3D experts provide spatially grounded region proposals, while 2D experts provide semantic cues for identifying object parts. The challenge is to integrate these complementary capabilities into a framework that can both produce meaningful part segmentations and progressively refine them. We present PartAgent, a training-free agentic framework for 3D part segmentation built upon two complementary modules: (i) Structural-Semantic Expert Integration combine…

items.title: AutoRL
items.summary: Reinforcement learning is a central step in improving model capabilities, but automating it is hard because training is unstable and needs constant supervision. Researchers from Meituan and collaborating universities introduce AutoRL, a multi-agent system that supervises a live RL run the way an RL researcher would, instead of following a fixed recipe.

items.title: Embodied AI Fails the Mirror Test: How a Simple Mirror Breaks Robot Policies
items.summary: Can a simple mirror expose the limitations of today's robotic manipulation policies? Inspired by the mirror self-recognition test in animal cognition, we investigate whether robot policies can reliably manipulate physical objects in scenes containing their reflections. We introduce RoboDojo-Mirror, a benchmark built on RoboDojo that preserves task objectives, success criteria, and policy checkpoints while comparing a mirror-free baseline with single-mirror, dual-mirror, and mirrored-tabletop conditions. Across five policies spanning Vision-Language-Action models, World Action Models, and agen…

items.source: dair-ai Top AI Papers of the Week (November 16 - November 22) - 2026
items.title: Weight-Space Programming
items.summary: Neural networks predict well, but in science the goal is often an explanation, and deep models rarely show which features drive their predictions. Researchers from Microsoft Research and colleagues introduce interpretable weight-space programming (iWSP), where an LLM agent builds models by writing their weights and features directly in code, with no gradient training.

items.title: ThinkMorph-SSL: Scaling Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning with Pretext Tasks
items.summary: People reason with pictures as well as words. Interleaved multimodal reasoning gives models a similar way to solve problems by creating intermediate images and using them to guide further reasoning. Training models with this ability usually relies on task-specific demonstrations, which are difficult to collect. We introduce ThinkMorph-SSL, a two-stage training recipe that uses images themselves as a source of supervision. The first stage, pretext reasoning, converts visual pretext tasks, such as image colorization and denoising, into instruction-free interleaved traces. Models describe a corr…

items.source: dair-ai Top AI Papers of the Week (November 16 - November 22) - 2026
items.title: GUARD
items.summary: Agents that edit their own harness without an external grader often get worse over time. Reflection and scalar scores mix up what an edit newly broke with what was never solved, which leads to local regressions, forgotten skills, and bloated memory. Google Cloud researchers propose GUARD, a framework for evolving a harness of prompts, skills, tool rules, and memory around a frozen base model without reference answers.

items.title: ICLWorld: Benchmarking In-Context Learning of Agents from Digital to Physical Worlds
items.summary: In-context learning (ICL) lets agents acquire new rules from context and adapt to user-specific requirements at inference time. The same frontier agents now operate both computers and robots, yet their ICL remains insufficiently assessed: existing benchmarks are largely offline, rely on text or static images, and risk training-data contamination, while robot evaluations are limited to method-level ablations. We present ICLWorld, an online benchmark that evaluates the ICL of agents from digital to physical worlds, covering computer use and robot use, together with UIverse, a unified harness th…

items.source: dair-ai Top AI Papers of the Week (November 16 - November 22) - 2026
items.title: EfficientSkill
items.summary: Skill optimizers usually add a new rule after every failure. The skill grows, the agent reads more tokens every turn, and long loops start to time out. Researchers from Google and Purdue University introduce EfficientSkill, which learns a skill for accuracy first and then prunes it for length.

items.title: Qwen-Image-HD: Autoregressive Diffusion for High Definition Image Generation
items.summary: Fine-tuning a generator on a complete high-resolution canvas requires long image sequences and substantial computation, yet local regions can still exhibit unnatural repetitive stripes when training resources are limited. We introduce Qwen-Image-HD, which adapts Qwen-Image 2.0 to high-resolution synthesis through local training and blockwise autoregressive generation. Each prediction covers a target tile at 1K scale, conditioned on high-resolution upper and left neighbors and a compressed historical thumbnail. These conditions provide adjacent fine-scale structures and an overview of the scen…

items.title: Safe Personal RSI
items.summary: A change to a personal assistant's instructions can improve how it handles tasks while also changing what it discloses, which requests it follows, and how it reports its actions. Researchers from CMU, UC San Diego, UC Berkeley, and other institutions build Safe Personal RSI, an update gate for Kicker, a personal health assistant.

items.title: CoT-Proxy: Cross-Format Transfer for Distilling Long-Horizon Policies
items.summary: Reasoning models become long-horizon agents through reinforcement learning or, more cheaply, through fine-tuning on a stronger teacher's trajectories, which contain the teacher's chain-of-thought as well as its actions. The standard fine-tuning approach imitates both, yet the strongest teachers are closed models whose chain-of-thought is hidden behind an API. We show that the chain-of-thought can be left out altogether and that the long-horizon policy can be distilled from the teacher's actions alone. The student is trained on these trajectories with its reasoning block left empty, while a KL…

items.title: CompoundingKernel
items.summary: Amazon researchers present CompoundingKernel, a self-improving agent system that writes GPU kernels by search. Over a thousand agents ran at once, and the resulting kernels rank first on the public L1, L2, and Quantization boards of SOL-ExecBench on NVIDIA B200.

items.title: Reinforcing Diffusion Models by Instantaneous Trajectory Distribution Matching
items.summary: Forward diffusion reinforcement learning (RL)---enabling deterministic ODE sampling without trajectory backpropagation---has grown increasingly popular for efficiently aligning diffusion models. However, we reveal that existing methods essentially rely on signed reward-weighted regression (RWR), regressing the trainable policy velocity onto rollouts from a behavior distribution. Unbiased baseline subtraction implicitly assumes that the policy velocity equals the behavior marginal velocity---an idealized assumption violated under classifier-free guidance (CFG) rollouts, offline/off-policy upda…

items.title: Against All Likelihood
items.summary: This essay from Meta argues that maximum likelihood, the dominant training principle for LLMs, is neither necessary nor sufficient for truth, since unlikely events happen every day and frequently repeated statements can be false. Drawing on philosophers who tie objectivity to invariance, including Nozick, Poincaré, and Cassirer, it proposes judging a statement true when it holds across relevant changes to the environment. The author connects this to work on out-of-distribution generalization, sketches how an LLM could test invariance at inference time, and discusses what it means for continua…

items.title: MAGPIE: Agentic Multi-Reference Image Generation via Executable Scene Construction
items.summary: Multi-reference image generation requires a model to preserve the appearance of selected subjects while arranging them according to an instruction. Despite recent progress in reference-based generation and compositional control, reliably organizing selected subjects into the intended scene remains challenging. Although existing methods provide various forms of compositional guidance, the planned relationships are not always explicitly instantiated for inspection and refinement before image synthesis. To address this limitation, we introduce MAGPIE, which represents the intended composition as…

items.title: Self-Directed Self-Improvement
items.summary: Researchers from MIT CSAIL and the University of Tübingen give a frozen model a compute budget and simple tools to write practice games, watch another copy of itself play them, and edit that copy's prompt and skill files, without real tasks, validation scores, or instructions on how to learn. Capable models built a working learning procedure on their own, with strategies such as calibrated task difficulty, controlled A/B comparisons, and self-built validation suites, and improved on held-out games with hidden mechanics. The text files they produced also improved play on external benchmarks wi…

items.title: Coding4Games: Can Modern Coding Agents Play Modern Video Games?
items.summary: Games, especially modern AAA games, challenge language models to perceive complex scenes, control actions, and make decisions over long horizons. Existing game benchmarks primarily test language models as computer-use agents that query a language model throughout play, incurring repeated inference cost and, in real-time games, acting while the environment continues to evolve. We ask whether coding agents can learn from game interaction to develop standalone game-playing programs that run without language model inference. We thus introduce Coding4Games, a benchmark for evaluating whether codin…

items.source: dair-ai Top AI Papers of the Week (November 16 - November 22) - 2026
items.title: QDA
items.summary: Researchers from MIT and NVIDIA present QDA, a system where an agent designs the post-training quantization recipe for each model and precision. It scores each candidate in minutes by its output KL divergence from the original model on reasoning traces the agent never sees, and draws on a shared library of public PTQ methods. Across four reasoning models, QDA beats the strongest public recipe by 0.9, 1.4, and 2.2 points at W4A16, W4A8, and W3A16 using 64 GPU-hours per search, and on GLM-5.3-Flash at NVFP4 W4A4 it recovers 98.3% of FP8 accuracy against 96.9% for the best vendor checkpoint.

items.title: VenusOCR2.0: Towards Efficient and Effective Document Parsing
items.summary: We present VenusOCR2.0, a compact 1B-parameter vision-language recognizer designed for both high-accuracy and high-throughput document parsing across text, tables, and formulas. items.summary: Autonomous specification engineering requires coding agents to translate functional requirements into executable tests and use the results to discover and validate defects. However, existing benchmarks evaluate coding agents on explicitly specified test generation tasks, commonly providing an issue description, a designated test entry point, or files to inspect, leaving the ability to determine what to test and where to investigate insufficiently evaluated. items.title: LoopDVR: Looped Transformer for Efficient Dense Visual Recognition
items.summary: We propose LoopDVR, a framework for converting pretrained Transformer-based dense visual recognition models into parameter-efficient looped networks. Rather than reducing the network width or depth directly, LoopDVR reuses Transformer blocks across layers in both the ViT backbone and Transformer decoder, reducing the number of parameters while retaining the original computational structure. However, naively sharing parameters can disrupt the distinct transformations learned at different depths. items.title: Residual Guidance for Real-Time Interactive Video Generation
items.summary: Real-time interactive video generation allows users to change the prompt during generation to steer the evolving video. However, existing streaming models, which generate videos chunk by chunk, often keep following the previous prompt after a switch. We trace this failure to context inertia, where the previous chunk acts as a strong prior that suppresses the new prompt.
